guarantees.claim: alert_fatal is asserted when any of shadowed_storage_err, alert_intg_err, sparse_fsm_error, counter_error, or control_integrity_error is high.

assumptions.claim: The hw2reg module correctly latches status_alert_recov_ctrl_update_err on its update strobe to capture the recoverable control update error.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect latching could cause the error to be missed or glitched, leading to undetected recoverable control update errors.

assumptions.claim: The error inputs to alert_fatal (shadowed_storage_err, alert_intg_err, sparse_fsm_error, counter_error, control_integrity_error) are synchronous to the sampling of alert_fatal or are held stable long enough to avoid glitch propagation.
assumptions.cond: when alert_fatal is observed by downstream logic
assumptions.risk: Combinational glitches may cause false assertion or missed capture of the fatal alert, breaking fault signaling.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational alert_fatal may glitch if its error inputs change asynchronously or have different arrival times, risking missed capture by the intended sticky status_alert_fatal_fault register.
uncertain_points.cond: error input transitions relative to the capture logic timing
uncertain_points.risk: A fatal alert could be missed, allowing critical integrity or fault conditions to go undetected.

uncertain_points.claim: Multiple fatal error sources are OR‑reduced to a single alert_fatal signal; it is unclear if each source has a separate sticky status bit for root‑cause isolation.
uncertain_points.cond: when any error source is active
uncertain_points.risk: Debug and fault isolation are hindered, especially for integrity and shadow storage errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The logic signal status_alert_fatal_fault is declared but not assigned in this chunk; its usage and connection to the alert_fatal path are not visible here.
uncertain_points.risk: If never assigned, fatal fault status would be missing, breaking the observability of fatal errors.
